 Learn more Microsoft ( MSFT ) reported its first quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines. 
 Microsoft stock rose more than 4% on the news. 
 For the quarter, Microsoft saw earnings per share (EPS) of $4.89 on revenue of $92.28 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $4.73 on revenue of $90.63 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. 
 The company saw EPS of $4.13 and revenue of $77.6 billion in the same period last year. 
 ( MSFT )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 531.01 -0.32 (-0.06%) At close: 4:00:01 PM EDT 554.00 +22.99 (+4.33%) After hours: 4:15:35 PM EDT Q1 marks the first quarter of Microsoft's new segment structure . 
 The Agents and Infra segment includes the revenue from Microsoft's Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud services, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions, and frontier and support services. 
 The Devices and Consumer segment includes sales tied to Microsoft's search and advertising businesses, Xbox, and Windows OEM and devices. 
 Agents and Infra revenue climbed to $76.8 billion, ahead of expectations of $75.6 billion, with Azure sales climbing 48% to $33.17 billion up from $22.38 billion in the same period last year. 
 Devices and Consumer sales totaled $15.5 billion. Wall Street was looking for $15 billion. 
 Capital expenditures, including leases, topped $39.37 billion, less than the $45.93 billion that analysts were anticipating.

 46 mins ago Jared Blikre The AI trade is back, and it's sorting software stocks into winners and losers
 October was the month investors gave this year's beaten-down software stocks a second chance. Four sessions later, they're taking it back and buying cybersecurity instead. 
 For most of October, the trade was easy to spot: Sell chips, buy software. Through the Oct. 22 close, the median stock in a 45-stock Yahoo Finance software basket was up about 13% for the month, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) had lost about 16%. 
 Then the trade flipped. Since that close, SOXX has jumped about 7%, and the First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF ( CIBR ) has gained about as much, while 26 of the 45 software stocks fell through Tuesday. 
 Change since the Oct. 22 close through Oct. 27, %. In parentheses: change from Sept. 30 to Oct. 22 · Yahoo Finance Since the Oct. 22 close, the 20 chip stocks in the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) have added nearly $570 billion in market value, according to Yahoo Finance calculations through Tuesday. The rest of the index lost about $40 billion. 
 "For now, early trading this week looks more like rotation within AI than a broad return of conviction," Vanda Research's Viraj Patel wrote Wednesday. 
 Software isn't breaking down. The equal-weight SPDR S&P Software & Services ETF ( XSW ) closed at a record on Monday. 
 Microsoft ( MSFT ), the biggest software name by market cap, reports after Wednesday's close . If its AI business keeps growing, the list of winners could get longer. Read more . 
 Today at 7:15 PM UTC Brian Sozzi Decoding Microsoft's AI workforce shake-up: Are more layoffs coming?
 Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi takes a closer look at Microsoft's ( MSFT ) employee buyouts on Sozzi Unleashed, examining the role of artificial intelligence in the tech giant's evolving workforce strategy. Sozzi breaks down what's driving the changes, how AI could reshape Microsoft's staffing needs, and whether another round of layoffs could be on the horizon. 
 Today at 7:00 PM UTC Daniel Howley Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on AI: 'Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us'
 After releasing its r evamped version of Copilot , Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the company will need to win users' trust. 
 "Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us," Nadella told Deirdre Bosa. Read more . 
 Today at 6:30 PM UTC Ines Ferré Tech rises for third day in a row ahead of Microsoft, Alphabet earnings
 Stocks edged higher for a third day in a row on Wednesday, ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision and earnings from Alphabet ( GOOG ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ). 
 The Tech (XLK ) sector advanced, extending gains as shares of chip giants Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), and Broadcom ( AVGO ) all rose. The move higher followed SK Hynix ( SKHY ), which saw  profits increase sevenfold last quarter . 
 Today at 6:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Microsoft to buyout to 60,000 employees
 Microsoft's earnings report comes just two days after Microsoft said it is offering buyouts to upward of 60,000 eligible employees as it seeks to reduce expenses amid its massive AI build-out. 
 "The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote in a memo to employees. 
 The company is reportedly offering buyouts to employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom, and the United States at level 70 and below, which includes some senior-level personnel. Read more .
